svg.font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, sans-serif
svg.text: The capability stack — and how fast each layer thinks
Each layer trusts the one below it to be faster than the problem it is solving. Colour marks how well each is verified today.

g.text: verified in water
verified on bench or real footage
built and tested in software, never flown
blocked on hardware or a firmware merge

svg.text: 2 ms per pass · runs with the Pi unplugged

g.text: attitude and heading hold
eight-thruster mixing, saturation kept in shape
failsafes: leak, battery, lost link, lost companion
depth hold — loop never closed in water
on-board move primitives, braked on board
self-tuning of the control gains

svg.text: 54 Hz through the ROS graph · 18 ms photon to detection

g.text: detection on a dedicated inference chip
segmentation, decoded without leaving integers
a visual lock that survives a blinking detector
flat-port refraction corrected, per camera
measured calibration — 46.7° in water
newest-frame camera path, 16.9 ms stale

svg.text: ESTIMATION — where am I, and am I moving
none of this existed on the old stack

g.text: velocity from the downward camera
height above the floor, from one pixel
an invariant filter fusing IMU, depth and flow
late measurements replayed at their true time
position fixes from a prop of known place
heading from lane lines and floor tiles

svg.text: MISSION — what to do, and when to give up

g.text: two vision verbs: centre on it, or drive to it
a run budget that skips what it cannot afford
task deadlines that abandon cleanly
payload fired mid-hold, on a fresh frame
evidence written beside every run
distance moves — waiting on a firmware merge

svg.text: Read it downward and it is a dependency chain: the mission can be slow because estimation is honest; estimation can be honest because
perception is calibrated; perception can be calibrated because the reflex layer holds the hull still enough to measure anything at all.
